source_english.description: Face Pull draws a rope toward the face with high elbows, ending in external rotation for the rear shoulders and upper back.
instructions: Set the cable at face height and hold the rope with both hands.
Step back, brace, and pull the rope toward the forehead.
Rotate the hands apart as the elbows travel behind the body.
Return slowly with the shoulders controlled.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to move the load.
source_english.safety_note: Use light cable resistance and stop before the shoulder rotation becomes forced.

source_english.description: Seated with the back supported, press the machine pads together to bring the thighs toward the midline.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the backrest.
Place your feet on the footrests and grasp the handles for stability.
Engage your adductor muscles and slowly bring your legs together, squeezing your inner thighs.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the pelvis against the pad while the knees move together.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: An iso-lateral low row uses independent machine handles pulled from a forward reach toward the lower ribs with the torso supported.
instructions: Adjust the seat and chest support so the handles start low and your shoulders are relaxed.
Grip both independent handles and brace your trunk against the support.
Pull the handles toward the lower ribs while drawing the shoulder blades back.
Pause briefly, then extend the arms under control without losing the chest position.
form_cues: Pull the elbows back close to the body.
Let each arm move through its own controlled range.
common_mistakes: Jerking the handles with the torso.
Cutting off the reach at the front.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load that lets both arms move evenly without twisting the torso.

source_english.description: Lat Pulldown (Cable) pulls the band, cable bar, or machine handles from overhead toward the upper chest while the torso stays braced.
instructions: Adjust the cable pulldown machine so that the seat is at a comfortable height and the knee pad is secured.
Sit on the seat with your back straight and your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the cable bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lean back slightly and engage your core.
Pull the cable bar down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the ribs stacked and shoulders down.
Drive the elbows toward the torso.
Control the return to the start.
common_mistakes: Leaning or swinging to move the load.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure station and a load or assistance level you can control through the full range.

source_english.description: Lat Pulldown (Machine) pulls the band, cable bar, or machine handles from overhead toward the upper chest while the torso stays braced.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your knees under the pads and your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Sit upright with your chest out and shoulders back, maintaining a slight arch in your lower back.
Pull the handles down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the ribs stacked and shoulders down.
Drive the elbows toward the torso.
Control the return to the start.
common_mistakes: Leaning or swinging to move the load.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure station and a load or assistance level you can control through the full range.

source_english.description: Lateral Raise (Machine) raises the hands or machine pads out to shoulder height in the frontal plane without swinging.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms straight.
Exhale and raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.
Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and stop if the shoulder cannot move smoothly.

source_english.description: Seated at the leg-extension machine, straighten the knees to lift the pad and lower it with control.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and backrest of the machine to fit your body.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet on the footpad.
Grasp the handles or sidebars for stability.
Extend your legs forward by straightening your knees, lifting the weight.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the thigh against the seat while the lower leg straightens.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: Preacher Curl (Machine) supports the upper arms on a preacher pad while the weight curls toward the shoulders and lowers fully.
instructions: Adjust the machine so the upper arms rest fully on the preacher pad.
Grip the handles underhand and keep the elbows planted.
Curl the handles toward the shoulders with the biceps.
Pause, then lower slowly to the starting position.
form_cues: Use a steady squeeze at the top.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a load that keeps the wrists and elbows aligned without momentum.

source_english.description: Pullover (Machine) moves the resistance from overhead toward the chest using a controlled shoulder-extension path.
instructions: Adjust the seat and handles of the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and grasp the handles with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms slightly bent and your core engaged.
Slowly pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your lats.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the elbows softly bent while the resistance travels from overhead toward the chest.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Cable) moves the arms outward and back through a controlled rear-delt fly arc while standing at the cable with a slight hip hinge.
instructions: Attach a D-handle to each low pulley cable and stand in the middle of the cable crossover machine.
Grasp the handles with a pronated grip (palms facing down) and take a step forward, positioning your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and lean forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your abs engaged.
With your arms extended out to the sides and slightly bent at the elbows, exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the cables back and upward in a reverse fly motion.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and stop if the shoulder cannot move smoothly.

source_english.description: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Machine) moves the arms outward and back through a controlled rear-delt fly arc with the chest supported on the machine pad.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms slightly bent.
Exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the handles back and outward, away from your body.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and stop if the shoulder cannot move smoothly.

source_english.description: With palms up on the straight bar, extend the elbows to push the cable down.
instructions: Attach the straight bar to the high pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grip the bar palms up and keep the elbows close to the ribs.
Push the bar down until the elbows are straight without moving the upper arms.
Pause, then return the bar slowly to the start.
form_cues: Keep the upper arms still while the elbows extend through the cable path.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: Sit with feet braced at the low pulley, grip the close V handle neutrally, and pull it toward the navel before extending the arms.
instructions: Sit at a low cable pulley with feet on the footplate, knees softly bent, and torso upright.
Hold the close V handle with palms facing each other.
Pull the handle to the navel while drawing both elbows behind the ribs.
Let the arms extend fully without rounding the back.
form_cues: Keep the chest supported or torso upright.
Drive the elbows toward the ribs.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest from the pad.
Shrugging instead of pulling the elbows.
Letting the weight fall on return.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the torso supported or upright so the shoulder is not jerked by the cable or bar.

source_english.description: Stair Machine (Floors) tracks climbing effort by the floors completed on a motorized stair machine.
instructions: Step onto the machine and select a manageable pace or floor target.
Climb by placing each foot fully on the next moving step.
Keep the trunk upright and use the rails only for balance.
Reduce the pace and stop the machine before stepping off.
form_cues: Look ahead rather than down constantly.
common_mistakes: Pulling the body with the rails.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the emergency stop accessible and choose a floor target that preserves safe foot placement.

source_english.description: Stair Machine (Steps) counts controlled alternating steps on a motorized stair machine.
instructions: Mount the machine and choose a comfortable step rate.
Alternate the feet onto the next steps with the whole foot supported.
Keep the torso tall and maintain a repeatable rhythm.
Slow the rate fully before stepping down from the machine.
form_cues: Keep the hips over the feet.
common_mistakes: Taking two steps at once unintentionally.
Stepping off while the pedals are moving.
source_english.safety_note: Use a pace that allows every step to be placed deliberately.

source_english.description: A standing leg curl on a machine bends one knee against a padded lever while the thigh stays vertical.
instructions: Adjust the machine pad behind one ankle and hold the support handles upright.
Keep the working thigh against the pad and bend the knee to draw the heel toward the glute.
Pause at the top without moving the hip.
Lower the lever slowly, complete the side, and switch legs.
form_cues: Point the knee toward the floor.
common_mistakes: Extending the hip to swing the lever.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load that lets the knee move smoothly without the pelvis rotating.

source_english.description: T Bar Row uses a chest-supported lever machine to pull a wide overhand handle toward the torso.
instructions: Adjust the chest pad and footplate so the sternum rests against the pad and both feet are planted.
Grip the handles slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip.
Pull the handles toward the lower ribs while keeping the chest on the pad.
Pause with the shoulder blades together, then lower until the arms lengthen.
source_english.safety_note: Set the pad and footplate before loading the machine and use a weight that keeps the chest supported.

source_english.description: Torso Rotation uses a seated torso-rotation machine to turn the trunk against resistance while the hips stay fixed.
instructions: Adjust the seat and thigh pads so the pelvis is supported and sit upright against the backrest.
Grip the handles at chest height and brace the abdomen.
Rotate the torso to the right until the machine reaches its comfortable endpoint.
Return to center, then repeat to the left without lifting the hips.
source_english.safety_note: Set the seat and pads securely and use resistance that permits a pain-free rotation.

source_english.description: Triceps Dip (Assisted) uses a kneeling counterweight platform to reduce the load during a parallel-bar dip.
instructions: Set the counterweight and kneel on the assistance pad with hands on the parallel handles.
Start with elbows straight and shoulders down.
Bend the elbows to lower until the upper arms approach parallel to the floor.
Press through the handles to return, then let the platform support the dismount.
source_english.safety_note: Choose enough assistance to control the entire dip and dismount with the platform still supported.

source_english.description: Triceps Extension (Machine) uses a seated lever pad and fixed handles to flex and extend the elbows.
instructions: Sit against the machine back pad with feet planted and handles held above the chest.
Grip the machine handles with an overhand grip and keep the upper arms fixed beside or above the torso.
Bend the elbows to lower the resistance to the forehead or behind the head.
Pause at the endpoint, then extend the elbows to return to straight arms.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load you can lower slowly and keep clear space around the head.

source_english.description: Triceps Rope Pushdown uses a high-pulley rope, extending both elbows while the rope ends separate slightly at the bottom.
instructions: Stand facing the high pulley with feet shoulder-width apart and knees softly bent.
Grip the rope with a neutral grip with elbows beside the ribs.
Press the attachment down until the elbows are straight without leaning over it.
Pause at the bottom, then allow the elbows to bend until the forearms return to the start.
source_english.safety_note: Set the pulley and attachment securely and use resistance that keeps the elbows close.
